summary: This article explains how the Olympic Games began in ancient Greece, how they were revived, what the rings mean, how the Paralympics began, and why training and fair play matter.
introduce: Give pairs four mixed-up steps of a simple task, such as making tea, and ask them to put the steps in order. Explain that “The Olympic Games: Then and Now” also follows an order, and good readers notice signal words like first, after, and finally.

keyTerms.def: a ring made of leaves or flowers
to bring something back to life or back into use

challengeTerms.def: an agreement to stop fighting for a period of time
to stand for or represent an idea
the process of helping someone recover after an injury or illness

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that playing fairly is more important than winning? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how the modern Olympic Games are similar to and different from the ancient Games.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review wreath, revive, and represent, and let weak readers put sentence strips of the main events in order before writing.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use truce, symbolize, and rehabilitation in a short paragraph that summarizes the key events in order and explain which step matters most.
